blocks.raw:
<Tip>
_Memory aid_: **"75% Rule"** — Hollow unit = net area < 75% of gross. Standard 6-inch CHB = 50% net = HOLLOW. **"BNA"** — **B**edded area (what contacts mortar), **N**et area (solid only), **A**rea gross (full bounding box). Bedded area determines bearing stress, not gross area.
</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={["Confusing net area with bedded area—net area is 100% solid material; bedded area is only the portion in actual mortar contact (typically 50–60% for hollow CHB).","Assuming all hollow units have the same net-to-gross ratio—while typical CHB is 45–55%, clay bricks may be 60–80%; always verify unit-specific data.","Using gross area for bearing stress calculations instead of bedded area—this underestimates stress and may lead to local crushing failures.","Treating the 75% threshold as a rough guideline instead of an absolute code criterion—75% is the exact dividing line: ≥75% is solid, <75% is hollow.","Specifying full-cell grouting to improve insulation—grouting eliminates insulation value and is structurally unnecessary where strategic grouting suffices.","Ignoring bedded area reduction in design—hollow units have 40–50% less bedded area than gross area; this significantly increases bearing stress and must be explicitly checked."]} />
